title: Mardonios comes down to the sea
prose: In the spring of **492 BC** **Darius** removes every other commander and gives the war to one man: **Mardonios**, son of **Gobryas**, young, and lately married to the king’s daughter **Artozostra**. He brings a very large land-army and a very large naval force down to **Kilikia**, puts the army on the road, and boards a ship himself.

title: Thasos, and then the mountain
prose: **Thasos** is taken without a hand raised in its defence. **Macedonia** is made to serve. Then the fleet crosses from **Thasos**, works along the coast to **Acanthos**, and tries to get round **Mount Athos** — and a violent north wind falls on it. THREE HUNDRED SHIPS AND MORE THAN TWENTY THOUSAND MEN. **Herodotus** itemises how they died: taken by the sea monsters that fill that water, dashed on the rocks, drowned not knowing how to swim, dead of the cold. He reports it as *it is said*, and the monsters arrive in the same breath as the arithmetic.

title: And the army fares no better
prose: While the fleet is dying at **Athos**, the land-army is camped in **Macedonia** and is attacked in the night by the **Brygian Thracians**. Many are killed and **Mardonios** himself is wounded. He will not leave until he has subdued them, and then leads the army home having lost heavily by both land and sea. THE FIRST EXPEDITION ENDS WITHOUT REACHING GREECE.

title: Remember the Athenians

He takes the command from **Mardonios**, who had failed, and gives it to **Datis** and **Artaphrenes**.

title: A fleet built for horses, and a route chosen out of fear
prose: They muster on the **Aleïan plain** in **Kilikia**, and the whole naval armament comes up to them — **six hundred triremes**, and with them the ships for carrying horses, WHICH DARIUS HAD ORDERED HIS TRIBUTARIES TO BUILD THE YEAR BEFORE. The horses go aboard, the army goes aboard, and they sail for **Ionia**. Then they do not coast the mainland. They cross from **Samos** by the **Icarian Sea** and go island to island — because, **Herodotus** thinks, they feared above all else the voyage round **Athos**. THE WRECK IS STILL DECIDING THE ROUTE TWO YEARS LATER.
